newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Wednesday at $63.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $65.00 but sales were seen at $64.00 by the end of the day, several feedlot sources said.
"If $64.00 comes, I think we'll see a lot of cattle move," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Trades at $64.00 would be steady with last week's active sales.
Prices were seen underpinned by firm beef values, but light beef movement and concern that beef may be near a top could keep fed cattle prices from reaching $65.00, they said.
Boxed beef prices on Tuesday were quoted up $0.45 to $0.57 for choice cuts and down $0.11 to $0.14 for select, with 243 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $103.09 per cwt, up $0.45 from Monday and up $4.05 since prices turned higher after the close July 10, USDA statistics showed.
